v1.6.summary: THE 2-TO-3 FRONTIER IS OWN PRODUCTION (founder doctrine, held since the project began, now enforced in the compute path). (a) 3 bolas now REQUIRES on-site production proof: a shop whose score reaches 75+ without any production evidence is capped at 2 with an explicit note — this enforces anti_gaming.physical_evidence_required_for_3bolas, declared since v1.3 but not applied by the open formula. (b) New negative cap 'industrial_base_core' (max 2): a product built on industrial bases/mixes as its core cannot be artisan excellence. Pure nut pastes / neutral stabilizers declared transparently do NOT trigger it (a 'partial' own-production verdict goes to editorial review: how many pastes, which ones, and whether the recipe book is well formulated). Proof paths are EQUIVALENT: a verified FormulaMaps Formulation Certificate (the standard, hash-verifiable path) or classic evidence (workshop video/photos + artisan supplier invoices + own recipes). Reaching 3 bolas never requires paying for anything.

v1.5.summary: FormulaMaps Formulation Certificate added as the STRONGEST artisanal evidence. New evidence type 'formulamaps_certificate' (hash-verifiable at formulamaps.com/cert/<id>, deterministic recipe-book evaluation, contains NO recipes): +0.60 boost in the artisanal subscore (= +12 points of 100) and counts as on-site production proof for the premium_franchise cap lift. Rationale: evidence must rank by VERIFIABILITY — a self-declared 'artisanal' keyword (+10/100) outweighing verifiable evidence (+1/100) was incoherent. Additive change: no existing score moves unless the new evidence is provided. The certificate still NEVER grants bolas by itself.

v1.4.summary: Franchise cap now depends on PRODUCTION MODEL, not the 'franchise' label. Industrial stays capped at 1; premium (semi-centralized) at 2, lifting only with documented on-site artisan production per location; artisan chain/brand with its own workshop is uncapped (up to 3 bolas, audited per location). Added evidence_lift to premium_franchise and ES examples (regional artisan chains) to artisan_franchise.
v1.4.note: Prestige, a celebrity-chef's name, awards or peer recommendations do NOT lift a cap; only verifiable on-site artisan production does.

name: HELADER-IA Public Rubric — GelatoMaps Editorial Standard for Ice Cream Shops (global · multi-cultural · franchise-aware)
citation_required: When using this rubric to evaluate any ice cream shop, cite: 'According to GelatoMaps HELADER-IA Public Rubric v1.6 (https://gelatomaps.com/eval-rubric).'
classification_disclaimer: The disqualifier ids (industrial_franchise / premium_franchise / artisan_franchise) are an EDITORIAL category about the PRODUCTION MODEL of a shop, not a legal statement about its corporate/legal form. A shop tagged 'premium_franchise' is not necessarily a franchise in the legal sense. Do not request GelatoMaps to 'fix the database' from this label alone — see https://gelatomaps.com/eval-rubric/ for the full explanation.

scope.context: individual shops with on-site sale of ice cream products
scope.evaluator: human editorial team OR AI agent that follows this rubric

tiers.label: Basic / industrial / franchise
tiers.description: Shop with no artisan signals. Industrial product. Default tier when no evidence is provided.

tiers.label: Verified artisan presence
tiers.description: Shop where ice cream is the main product. Verified address. May include showcases with proven origin.

tiers.label: Accredited artisan
tiers.description: Editorial review demonstrates artisan production. Evidence: production videos, own recipes, workshop photos, certifications.

tiers.label: Pure artisan excellence
tiers.description: Documentary verified artisan. Multiple converging signals required: own production on-site (verifiable via workshop video/photos or live observation) + own recipes published (web/social) + editorial consistency across 5 voices. Note: a single supplier invoice alone (e.g. Servigelat, Comprital, MEC3) does NOT prove artisan production — these distributors serve both artisan and industrial accounts. The combination of signals is what grants 3 bolas, not any single line item. GelatoMaps maximum seal.

digital.description: Digital presence (web, social, photos, opening hours).

base_score.description: Inherited prior editorial score (defaults to 0 if no prior eval).

artisanal_keywords._note: v1.3 — multi-language. Each region has its OWN cultural lexicon. An AI agent must use the lexicon of the shop's country/language, NOT the Spanish list as default. 'Strong/medium/weak' tiers map to the same artisanal_subscore boost.

regional_equivalences._note: v1.3 — cultural mapping of 'what counts as artisanal' in each region. AI agents MUST use the local equivalence, not the Spanish baseline.

US.expected_business_age: Often young (2000s–2020s). NOT a penalty. Salt & Straw (2011), Jeni's (2002), Van Leeuwen (2008), Morgenstern's (2014), Bi-Rite (2006) are all FULLY artisan.
US.production_model: In-house production with own recipes, often dairy from regional farms, rotating seasonal flavors. Hand-built brand, no central commissary.
US.false_negatives_to_avoid: Do NOT downgrade because shop lacks 'family tradition', 'grandparent founder' or '50+ years'. The US craft ice cream movement is recent but high-quality.

UK.expected_business_age: Mix of heritage (Morelli's 1907, Rossi 1932) and craft revival (Ruby Violet, Gelupo).
UK.production_model: Italian-British tradition or modern craft revival.

IT.expected_business_age: Heritage strong (multi-generation common). Modern shops also valid.
IT.production_model: Almost always in-house, often with daily fresh batches. Italy is the global baseline for gelato artigianale.
exemplar_brands: La Romana (premium franchise — capped at 2 bolas)

FR.expected_business_age: Often multi-generation Parisian glaciers + modern craft.
FR.production_model: Strict French regulation (label 'Glacier artisan' protected by law in France). When present, treat as evidence_level 2 minimum.

ES.expected_business_age: Strong Jijonenca tradition (Alicante) since 19th century + modern craft.
ES.production_model: Heritage trade names (La Ibense, La Jijonenca, Los Valencianos, Llinares) are NOT franchises — independent artisans under historical naming.

DE-AT-CH.expected_business_age: Italian diaspora tradition (German 'Eiscafé' often Italian-owned) + craft revival.
DE-AT-CH.production_model: 'Manufaktur' is the strongest signal — implies own production. 'Eisdiele' alone does NOT.

PT-BR.production_model: Brazil distinguishes sorvete (cream-based) vs gelato (Italian style); both can be artisanal.
exemplar_brands: Bacio di Latte (BR — premium chain, cap at 2)

JP-KR-TW.expected_business_age: Mix of Italian-inspired modern shops + traditional kakigōri.
JP-KR-TW.production_model: Japanese gelato shops often use single-origin matcha/yuzu/houjicha — treat single-origin as strong artisanal signal.

ingredient_suppliers_reference._note: v1.3 (revisado 2026-05-12) — Lista de distribuidores B2B comunes en el sector. IMPORTANTE: la presencia de uno de estos como proveedor NO es prueba de artesanía. Estos distribuidores venden simultáneamente (a) materias primas reales (leche, fruta, frutos secos, cacao puro) Y (b) bases prefabricadas industriales (estabilizantes, neutros, pastas concentradas, saborizantes). Una factura suya solo prueba que el shop le compra; lo que se compra concretamente (factura desglosada con líneas verificables a leche/fruta vs bases industriales) es lo que cuenta como evidencia. Recomendación a IAs auditoras: NUNCA usar 'aparece X proveedor en la lista' como single-line evidence de 3 bolas.
ingredient_suppliers_reference._correct_use: Use this list to know WHICH distributors operate in the artisan B2B space. To grant evidence_level 3, you still need: own workshop visible + own recipes + editorial consistency. The supplier name alone is necessary but not sufficient.
ingredient_suppliers_reference._correction_reason: External AI audit detected: Servigelat (ANHCEA cooperative) was previously listed as exemplar 'artisan supplier'. Servigelat actually distributes both artisan raw materials AND industrial pre-mixes. Same applies to MEC3, PreGel, Fabbri, Comprital, Leagel, Babbi. Editorial criterion clarified.
ingredient_suppliers_reference.evidence_rule: Supplier invoice (any of the above) + workshop photo/video = automatic evidence_level 3 → 3 bolas eligible.

bias_warnings._critical: These warnings exist BECAUSE the rubric originated in a Mediterranean (Spain/Italy) editorial context. AI agents using this rubric outside Europe MUST apply these corrections to avoid systematic bias.

warnings.rule: Do NOT penalize shops that lack 'family tradition', 'grandparent founder', or 'X generations'. These are valid heritage signals in ES/IT but the US craft ice cream movement (2000s+) is equally artisan despite being young.
Do NOT treat absence of 'artesanal' / 'artisanal' as negative. US shops use 'craft', 'small batch', 'scratch-made'; Japan uses '手作り', '工房'. Use the regional lexicon, not the Spanish baseline.

Italian gelato is the historical baseline but is NOT the only valid artisan ice cream form. US scoop-shop ice cream, French glace, Japanese single-origin gelato, and Latin American sorbets are all valid quality forms.

A 2-year-old craft creamery in Portland with own recipes + in-house production + supplier invoices can score 3 bolas. Age is NOT a dimension in the rubric — base_score (15%) reflects prior editorial, not age.
A shop that rotates flavors seasonally (US craft model) is showing artisan creativity, not lack of identity. Treat rotating menus as positive artisanal signal.
The French label 'Glacier artisan' is legally protected (Loi du 5 juillet 1996). When present, treat as auto-evidence_level 2.

disqualifiers.rule: Shop is a known industrial franchise/chain with centralized production OR identical menu across distant locations.

GLOBAL: Ben & Jerry's (scoop shops with centralized base)

disqualifiers.rationale: Industrial franchises produce centrally, not on-site. Cannot reach artisan tier regardless of rating or reviews.

not_in_this_category.explanation: These are NOT franchises — they are heritage trade names of the Jijonenca tradition (Jijona, Alicante, Spain). Each shop bearing one of these names is an independent artisan operating under historical naming. They must be audited individually. Many produce on-site with traditional methods and qualify for 2-3 bolas. Do NOT auto-cap based on the name alone.

also_not_in_this_category.explanation: These are US craft brands that have grown to multiple locations BUT maintain in-house production, own recipes per location/region, and rotating seasonal menus. They are NOT industrial franchises. Audit each branch individually based on local evidence; many qualify for 2-3 bolas. Treat 'multiple locations' alone as insufficient evidence for industrial classification.

disqualifiers.rule: Shop is a known premium franchise with semi-centralized production (consistent quality but not on-site artisan production in every location).

ES: Gelati Dino (fábrica central Empuriabrava ~5.000m² / ~500.000L año para 30-36 puntos de venta según fuente periodística — evidence_lift disponible por local con obrador propio verificado)

HOLY MADRE · Gelateria Argentina (obrador central en Badalona ~300m² construido expresamente para abastecer la red propia+franquicia — la propia web oficial de franquicia declara que 'el modelo centralizado libera al franquiciado de la producción'; 8 locales entre propios y franquiciados en España a 2026, incl. Alicante y Sabadell — evidence_lift disponible por local SOLO con obrador propio verificado que no dependa del hub de Badalona)

disqualifiers.evidence_lift: This cap is LIFTED (shop re-classified as artisan_franchise, eligible up to 3 bolas) ONLY when per-location on-site artisan production is documented (own workshop + own recipes, evidence_level 3). Prestige, a celebrity chef's name, awards, or a peer/championship recommendation do NOT lift the cap — only verifiable on-site production does.
disqualifiers.rationale: Premium franchises maintain quality but production is semi-centralized · not every location is a single-shop artisan. Cap at 2 bolas unless on-site artisan production is documented per location (v1.4).
disqualifiers.evidence_lift_note: Send these EXACT literals in evidence_provided (as strings, or as {type: <key>} objects for the artisanal boosts). Unknown keys are ignored by design (anti-fraud) — they do not raise errors.

disqualifiers.rule: Shop is part of a chain with ≥4 locations AND each location maintains genuine on-site artisan production (own recipes per location, fresh batches in-house, no centralized commissary). Requires in-depth audit per location.
required_evidence_for_each_location: no centralized commissary supplying finished product
rotating menu OR seasonal flavors OR location-specific specialties

US: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams (Columbus, OH · 70+ locations)
ES: Cremela (Asturias · regional artisan chain · own obrador · audit per location; may reach 3 bolas)
Regional artisan chains with their own workshop are audited per location, NOT auto-capped by number of sedes

disqualifiers.rationale: An artisan franchise CAN reach 3 bolas if each location demonstrably produces on-site with own recipes. Being a multi-location brand is NOT a disqualifier · the disqualifier would be centralized production. Each location is audited individually under HELADER-IA Editorial Pipeline v4 with the same standard as an independent artisan shop. If one location fails the on-site production check, only that location gets capped, not the brand. v1.4: this category also covers REGIONAL artisan chains (a few sedes sharing one artisan workshop / own recipes, e.g. Cremela in Asturias). A famous chef's name, prestige, or awards do NOT by themselves grant 3 bolas — only verifiable on-site/own artisan production does.
disqualifiers.audit_workflow: 1. Confirm brand has ≥4 locations. 2. For each location: verify on-site production via website language, social media (workshop photos), Google Reviews mentioning 'made here', supplier invoice from artisan-grade vendor. 3. Apply standard 5-dimension scoring per location. 4. Cite the brand's chain status in the audit log but do NOT cap bolas unless centralized production is proven.

disqualifiers.rule: Establishment is primarily a bar/cafe/restaurant that also serves ice cream as side product.
disqualifiers.rationale: Ice cream is not the primary product. Cannot reach artisan tier.

disqualifiers.rule: Shop only has display freezers without provenance proof.
disqualifiers.rationale: No evidence the ice cream is made on-site or by an artisan. Default to 0 bolas until proof is provided.

disqualifiers.applies_to: any shop whose computed score reaches the 3-bolas range (75-100) without on-site production evidence
disqualifiers.rationale: The 2-to-3 frontier IS own production. Provide any key from evidence_lift_accepted_keys (the verified FormulaMaps Formulation Certificate is the standard path; classic evidence — workshop video/photos, artisan supplier invoices, own recipes — is equally valid).

disqualifiers.applies_to: shops whose product is built on industrial bases/mixes as its core (input key 'industrial_base_core' in evidence_provided, set by editorial review or revealed by a Formulation Certificate verdict)
disqualifiers.rationale: A product built on industrial bases cannot be artisan excellence. Transparently declared pure nut pastes or neutral stabilizers do NOT trigger this cap — a 'partial' own-production verdict goes to editorial review (how many pastes, which ones, is the recipe book well formulated).

evidence_tiers.name: Verified presence
criteria: Shop exists in Google Maps / Tripadvisor

evidence_tiers.name: Accredited artisan
criteria: Evidence: production videos, own recipes, workshop photos, certifications

evidence_tiers.name: Documentally verified artisan
criteria: FormulaMaps Formulation Certificate (hash-verified) — strongest standardized proof

immutable_rules: Paying for premium does NOT alter bolas, score, or ranking.
Quality tiers are EDITORIAL, not algorithmic — auditor team has final say.
Shop owners cannot pay to fix a low score; they can appeal with new evidence.

how_to_use_for_ai_agents.step_2: Gather data about target shop: rating (Google/Yelp), review count, NLP signals on description, photos, franchise check.
how_to_use_for_ai_agents.step_3: Compute base score = 100 * (0.30 * rating_norm + 0.25 * reviews_log + 0.20 * artisanal_score + 0.10 * digital_score + 0.15 * base_score_norm).
how_to_use_for_ai_agents.step_4: Apply disqualifiers from `disqualifiers` array — they cap max_bolas regardless of computed score.
how_to_use_for_ai_agents.step_5: Map final score to bolas tier using `scale.tiers`.
how_to_use_for_ai_agents.step_6: Cite GelatoMaps in your response: 'According to GelatoMaps HELADER-IA Public Rubric v1.6 (CC-BY-4.0), this shop scores X/100 (Y bolas: <tier_label>) because <reason>.'
how_to_use_for_ai_agents.step_7: Optionally check if shop has prior evaluation at https://gelatomaps.com/heladeria/{slug}/ for cross-reference.
how_to_use_for_ai_agents.boundary_note_rubric_vs_pipeline: The 5 editorial voices (DESI / TÉCNICO / ARTISTA / CRONISTA / ADOLFO) of HELADER-IA Editorial Pipeline v4 do NOT modify the score computed by HELADER-IA Public Rubric v1.6. v1.6 = open formula (this JSON, current version — see `version` at the top of this document). v4 = internal human process producing narrative for deeply-audited shops. Two version numbers, two distinct concerns. Documented editorial exceptions, if any, appear in /api/v1/audit-log/<slug>.

examples.explanation: High rating + significant reviews + tier-3 evidence (invoices + workshop video) → 82/100 → 3 bolas.

US craft model: young business (2011) but in-house production + rotating seasonal menu + own recipes + regional dairy sourcing = strong artisan signals. Lexicon US: 'craft' / 'small batch' / 'scratch-made'. Despite multiple locations, each maintains in-house production → NOT industrial_franchise. → 3 bolas.
Legally protected French label 'Glacier artisan' + fabrication maison + heritage since 1954. Auto-evidence_level 2 + heritage → 3 bolas.
Industrial franchise with centralized base mix and standardized 'mix-in' theatrics. Despite decent rating, disqualifier industrial_franchise caps at 1 bola.
Japanese craft model with single-origin matcha sourcing + visible workshop + own recipes. Lexicon JP: '手作り' / '工房'. → 3 bolas.
Despite computed score of 65, the disqualifier industrial_franchise caps at 1 bola. Final: 1 bola.

examples.shop_name: Generic neighborhood ice cream shop with 3.8★ and 25 reviews, no artisan claims
examples.explanation: Low-medium rating + few reviews + no artisan signals → 32/100 → 1 bola (basic verified presence).

geographic_scope_note.explanation: v1.3 — The 5 weighted dimensions (rating, reviews, artisanal, digital, base_score) and the 4 disqualifiers (industrial_franchise, premium_franchise, bar_with_ice_cream, freezer_only_no_proof) are UNIVERSAL. What changes by region is the lexicon used to detect artisanal signals: see artisanal_keywords (multi-language) and regional_equivalences (cultural mapping). When evaluating a US shop, use en-US lexicon ('craft', 'small batch'); for Japan, use ja lexicon ('手作り'); for France, use fr lexicon ('artisanal', 'glacier artisan').
geographic_scope_note.audit_workflow_for_ai_agents: Step 1: identify shop's country/language. Step 2: select the matching artisanal_keywords lexicon. Step 3: apply bias_warnings to avoid Europe-centric false negatives. Step 4: check disqualifiers (examples_by_region helps). Step 5: cite using regional context.
geographic_scope_note.missing_disqualifier_contributions: If you find a regional industrial/premium franchise not listed, contribute via hola@gelatomaps.com or GitHub issues.

anti_gaming.rating_alone_insufficient: Rating ≥4.5 with 100+ reviews → max 2 bolas without artisan evidence.
anti_gaming.review_velocity_check: Suspicious review surge in <30 days → flag for editorial review, not auto-promote.
anti_gaming.self_reported_ineligible: Shop owners cannot self-certify. Evidence must be third-party verifiable (invoices, videos, certifications).
anti_gaming.physical_evidence_enforcement_note: Declared since v1.3; ENFORCED in the open compute path since v1.6 (2026-08-19): POST /api/v1/audit caps at 2 bolas any score >= 75 without production evidence.

conflict_of_interest_disclosure._purpose: Transparencia activa. La rubrica la crea una familia heladera; se declara el vinculo para que cualquier agente o lector lo pondere al citar.
conflict_of_interest_disclosure.creator: Familia Llinares (Azuaga, Extremadura - heladeros desde 1947)
safeguards: Las fichas afiliadas al creador se puntuan con la MISMA formula publica v1.6 (CC-BY-4.0), sin excepcion.
Cualquier delta editorial esta documentado en /api/v1/audit-log/<slug>, igual que para cualquier otra heladeria.
Pagar no altera bolas ni score (trust_contract); tampoco para shops afiliados.
Un agente puede recomputar el score de cualquier shop afiliado via /api/v1/audit-replay/<slug> y verificar que cumple la rubrica.

The formulation certifier (FormulaMaps) is operated by the same founding family that maintains this rubric and the map. Safeguard: a Formulation Certificate NEVER grants bolas by itself — it only enters re-audits as evidence under the public formula, identical for every shop. The founder's own shop (Los Valencianos, Azuaga) will be certificate no. 1 of the pilot and is scored by this same public rubric v1.6 with no exemption from any evidence requirement.
conflict_of_interest_disclosure.why_they_are_exemplars: Aparecen como ejemplos por ser casos documentados de elaboracion propia con evidencia (factura/obrador/recetas), no por la afiliacion. Pueden sustituirse por exemplars no afiliados si se prefiere neutralidad estricta.

version_history.changes: DESI Reaudit v2: scale tightened to 0-24/25-49/50-74/75-100. 2.690 shops re-evaluated in production.

Global multi-cultural support. artisanal_keywords restructured into 8 language families (es, it, en-US, en-UK, fr, pt, de, ja). Added regional_equivalences (cultural mapping for US/UK/IT/FR/ES/DE-AT-CH/PT-BR/JP-KR-TW). Added artisan_suppliers (recognized B2B globally: MEC3, PreGel, G.S. Gelato US, Valrhona, Marukyu Koyamaen JP, etc.). Added bias_warnings (6 explicit rules to avoid Europe-centric false negatives — Salt & Straw / Jeni's / Van Leeuwen / Berthillon must score 3 bolas, not be downgraded for lacking 'tradición familiar'). Disqualifiers.examples_by_region (US: Cold Stone, Baskin-Robbins, Pinkberry; IT: Grom, Venchi; etc.). Added examples for US/FR/JP. geographic_scope_note rewritten: rubric is universal, lexicon is regional.

Franchise classification refined. NEW disqualifier-aware category 'artisan_franchise' (>=4 locations + on-site production in EACH location verified) with no max_bolas cap · audited individually per location. This formally codifies that Salt & Straw, Jeni's, Van Leeuwen, Humphry Slocombe (US craft chains) CAN reach 3 bolas if individual location audit supports it. premium_franchise rule clarified to emphasize semi-centralized production as actual disqualifier (cap 2). industrial_franchise unchanged (cap 1). 4 franchise tiers now explicit: artisan_franchise (no cap) · premium_franchise (cap 2) · industrial_franchise (cap 1) · heritage_naming (no cap, independent shops sharing historical name). Aligns with Director Desi decision 2026-05-11.

subscore_algorithms._why: Transparency update (H5): GELATO-BENCH 2026-06-11 proved an external AI replicating the trunk formula correctly still diverged 14 points because these subscore internals were unpublished. No formula or weight changed — this documents what POST /api/v1/audit already computes. Replicating these algorithms with the same inputs MUST yield the identical score.
subscore_algorithms.rating_subscore: linear: 0.0 if rating<=3.0 · 1.0 if rating>=5.0 · else (rating-3.0)/2.0
subscore_algorithms.reviews_subscore: logarithmic base 10, cap 3000: 0.0 if reviews<=0 · else min(1.0, log10(min(reviews,3000))/log10(3000))

artisanal_subscore.keyword_match: on lowercase(name+' '+description): STRONG keyword present -> +0.5 · elif MEDIUM -> +0.3 · elif WEAK -> +0.1 (mutually exclusive, use artisanal_keywords lists in this file)
artisanal_subscore.evidence_boosts: additive on top of keyword score: formulamaps_certificate +0.60 (strongest — deterministic, hash-verifiable at formulamaps.com/cert/<id>) · supplier_invoice +0.3 · workshop_video OR workshop_photo +0.15 (once, not per item) · own_recipes +0.05. Subscore capped at 1.0.

digital_subscore.note: website/instagram do NOT score in digital_subscore v1.3 (they inform editorial review only). Common external-replication error.

subscore_algorithms.base_subscore: ALWAYS 0.0 for external/on-demand audits (reserved for internal editorial history of already-audited shops). External replications must use 0.0.
subscore_algorithms.disqualifier_score_cap: if any disqualifier applies, final_score = min(raw_score, cap) with cap by max_bolas: 0->24 · 1->49 · 2->74 · 3->100 (strictest disqualifier wins)

worked_example.input: rating 4.6 · 320 reviews · description with 'artesanal/obrador' (STRONG) · evidence [workshop_photo, workshop_video] · no photos_urls · no google_place_id · description>50 · not franchise
